newsitem.title: FINLAND: Ageing ships a headache in metal shipping.
newsitem.headline: Ageing ships a headache in metal shipping.

text.p: Ageing world fleets have become a serious headache in transporting metal concentrates, a shipping manager for Portugal's Somincor mining company said at the Metal Bulletin base metal concentrates conference on Thursday.
Sominco charters 50 to 60 vessels a year to export 550,000 dry tonnes of copper concetrates from its Neves Corvo mine, Jose Rui da Silva told delegates.
But locating the right size vessel, not more than 15 years old with a reliable owner, is increasingly difficult.
Using an overaged vessel requires extra insurance tax of around 0.4 percent of the total value of the cargo, he said.

"The world fleet is getting older and older and not so many shipowners are willing to spend about $15 million on a new building vessel knowing from the beginning that the market will not guarantee them the real income to cover the cost," he said.
